blocking.issue: P9 calls every remote-dependency failureMode default 'overridable' and then lists authentication and authorization as examples. The Configuration Model Policy type registry makes auth.*, authz.* and auth/authz-class plugin Policies 'closed only': setting failureMode: open on them is RZ-CFG-029. So the binding principle contradicts the owning document on a security-relevant default.
blocking.evidence: L178 (P9): "Each Policy type with a remote dependency has a documented, overridable default `failureMode`: authentication and authorization fail closed, Rate Limits fail open"; configuration model Policy registry: "| `auth.jwt`, `auth.api-key`, `auth.basic`, `auth.mtls` | auth | ... | closed; closed only |", "| `authz.cel` | ... | closed; closed only |"; configuration model: "Authentication and authorization types ... are `closed` only: `open` there is RZ-CFG-029".
blocking.fix: Reword the second sentence of P9 to: "Each Policy type with a remote dependency has a documented default `failureMode`, overridable only where the [Configuration model](../architecture/02-configuration-model.md#policy) registry allows: authentication and authorization always fail closed, and Rate Limits fail open by default ([ADR-0008](../adr/0008-rate-limiting-local-bucket-and-gcra.md))."

blocking.issue: P6 describes a Gateway-level cap on aggregate Plugin memory per Node, but no such field exists. The Gateway sketch in the Configuration Model lists its limits in full (maxRequestBodyBytes, maxRequestHeaderBytes, maxResponseBodyBytes, maxCompositionSteps, maxBufferedBytes) and says 'A field not shown does not exist; other documents propose new fields through Open questions.' P6 also lists Plugin limits as 'memory pages, execution deadline, host-call quotas'. The Plugin sketch defines only `limits: {memoryBytes, timeout}`, and host-call quotas have no field. Because every document inherits P6, this commits the Configuration Model to fields it does not define.
blocking.evidence: L175 (P6): "declared limits (memory pages, execution deadline, host-call quotas); ... A Gateway-level cap bounds aggregate Plugin memory per Node; reaching it refuses new instances and never crashes the Node."; configuration model Plugin sketch: "limits: {memoryBytes: 16Mi, timeout: 5ms}"; configuration model Gateway sketch `limits` block (no Plugin memory field); configuration model: "A field not shown does not exist".
blocking.fix: Reword P6 to: "Plugins run in a WASM sandbox with deny-by-default Capabilities and declared limits (`memoryBytes`, `timeout`; further limits are owned by [WASM plugin system](../architecture/05-wasm-plugin-system.md)); within them, a faulty Plugin fails its own Filter, not the Node. A Node-wide cap on aggregate Plugin memory (field: OQ-vision-and-positioning-14) refuses new instances when reached and never crashes the Node." Add OQ-vision-and-positioning-14: "Where is the Node-wide aggregate Plugin memory cap declared?" | Gateway `limits` field (Configuration model amendment); `RURALZ_*` process setting; fixed default | WASM plugin system owner | No.

non_blocking.suggestion: P3 says remote calls such as a Semantic Cache embedding call are "declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode`". The Policy kind defines `failureMode` and `stateStoreTimeout` but no generic timeout. The Configuration Model says `ai.semantic-cache` "uses the selected AIModel's cache.semantic parameters", and no field names an embedding `AIProvider`. The Open source and business model bullet about "a local embedding `AIProvider` such as `ollama`" has the same gap. Consider: "... are declared in configuration with a deadline and the Policy's `failureMode` (fields owned by [AI/LLM gateway](../architecture/06-ai-llm-gateway.md))".

P8 says "`max_tokens` (or a Policy default cap)". The Configuration Model already defines the cap as `AIModel.spec.limits.maxOutputTokens`, and `ai.token-budget` fixes only `consumerQuota`. Use "`max_tokens` (or the AIModel's `limits.maxOutputTokens`)" so the principle does not imply a new Policy field.

P4 says "(file and OCI mode need none)". The System Overview has three deployment modes, and OCI pull is part of file mode, not a separate mode. Write "(file mode, directory or OCI pull, needs none)".

Exit rule: "Nodes re-enroll while Last-Known-Good keeps traffic flowing." According to P9 and System Overview Figure 5, a detached Node keeps serving its active Revision and boots Last-Known-Good only after a restart. Write "Nodes re-enroll while they keep serving their active Revision (Last-Known-Good after a restart)."
